items: Coaching progress: the filter row lost its padding when it moved inside the panel (Champion was hugging the edge), and the "Selected accounts · all roles" note sat on the bottom edge instead of centred — both fixed
Sort the coaching periods oldest-first or newest-first with the new ↑/↓ button; the choice is remembered, and the ▲/▼ comparisons still read against the previous period either way

Coaching progress is one page again, and one table: each row is the stretch after a coaching session, so expanding it shows that session's notes, coach and clips right above the metrics that followed. No more two lists of the same sessions, and no third row of tabs
The Baseline row stays as your pre-coaching reference, and the champion/queue/side filters moved inside the panel they actually filter
Adding a session is a popup, reachable from the panel header instead of a form buried under the session list. Editing uses the same popup, with the notes as a full Markdown editor

Sessions can record who coached them. The field is optional, can be filled in on older sessions afterwards, and remembers coaches you've used so you can pick them again — removing one from those suggestions never changes the sessions that already name them

Fixed: a block that a new series had already finished still showed the "active" badge, so it looked open while offering no Close early — it now reads "finished with series", and "active" is reserved for the block your next game actually lands in (a full block no longer claims it either)

Recordings get an event timeline: every kill, death, assist, structure and objective sits where it happens on the video — click one to jump straight there. The itemised list is still there behind an "Event list" toggle, collapsed by default

Reflection tags are suggestions, not analysis: your chosen tags sit on their own row, and at most three are offered under "Suggested for this game" — only things plainly true from the numbers ("Won lane, lost game", "High deaths"), never a guess at how you played. Everything else is what the free-text tag and the note are for
Reflection tags read properly capitalised, and a tag you've picked no longer renders dark-on-dark
The heatmap legend reads kills, deaths, assists, towers, objectives
Recordings now show up on the games list under Coach → Coaching progress too, not just Overview and Blocks
Fixed: a block game's expanded panel showed the Side picker twice
The Lane result and Side pickers now name what "Auto" resolves to — "Ahead (Auto)", "Strong Side (Auto)" — instead of just saying Auto
Blocks: the current block's header gets a "+ Game" button opening the recent-games list in a popup — the picker at the foot of the page is a long scroll away once you have a few blocks

Stats now cover every role, not just top lane — your lane opponent is whoever played your position. Set a main/secondary role in Settings and use the new Role filter to narrow any view. Thanks to @bs1phc
Death map (Trends): a schematic Rift heatmap of where you die, built from match timelines. Thanks to @bs1phc
Full-game gold/CS/XP/level curve per game, so you can see where a lead appeared or evaporated. Thanks to @bs1phc
Per-game reflection tags plus a freeform note, kept separate from block learnings and matchup notes. Thanks to @bs1phc

Ascent VOD integration: link your local recordings to games, jump straight to a death, and chapter them automatically. Uploading to YouTube is optional — install requirements-youtube.txt for one-click upload, or use the manual path that opens the file for you. Thanks to @bs1phc
Research players moved out of Settings into their own view under Prepare, and the top bar became a rounded card with roomier nav. Thanks to @bs1phc
Fixed: hiding Series, Champion pool or Tier list in Settings → Visible tabs failed the whole save with an error

Settings: fixed a broken Recordings & YouTube / Backup section — the merge had left two overlapping copies of the backup controls, so half the page rendered wrong and the second Import button did nothing
The YouTube upload button only appears once upload is actually set up; otherwise a small ℹ explains how to enable it and takes you to Settings
The Ascent scan result moved into a popover on the 🎬 button instead of a long line of text that wrapped the top bar onto a second row

Player comparison is no longer stuck in the Playbook — the ⧉ button now also sits on every Matchups row, on each champion in My champions, and on Coaching progress (which compares totals, not per-session segments)

The comparison window shows YOUR stats as the first column, so it's actually side by side. It also opens much wider, and defaults to a roomy comparison table — stats down the side, players across the top, with the best value in each row marked (fewer deaths counts as better). "Compact view" switches back to the dense card layout
My champions has a column picker: kills/deaths/assists, gold per minute, damage per minute and average game length are all available beyond the default six

Fixed: the desktop app was throwing away every saved UI preference when you closed it — column choices, collapsed blocks, saved skill grids, the view each section reopens on. The native window ran in private mode, so nothing the app remembered survived a restart. It now keeps that state next to your database
Every column picker gets a "Reset to defaults" option, so you can get back to the standard columns without un-ticking them one at a time
Column pickers are now a ▥ icon button instead of the "Columns" text, matching the other icon controls in the header rows

New Series view (Coach → Series): every challenge on one page — its goals, what each block in it taught you, and how it actually went. Each series gets closing notes: did you hit the goals, what actually changed, what's next

The top bar is now grouped into three sections — Analyze (Overview, Matchups, Trends), Coach (Coaching progress, Blocks, Champion pool) and Prepare (Playbook, Tier list, Research) — with the section's views on a second row. Each section remembers the view you last used in it, and 1/2/3 jump between sections. The bar is sticky, so it stays reachable down a long page
Champion pool is its own view under Coach instead of a field buried in Settings — it's a commitment you revise, not app configuration. The ✎ on the Blocks page opens it directly
"Matchup guide" is now called "Playbook", so it stops reading like the Matchups stats tab it sits next to
Every view can be deep-linked by URL again, including the Tier list (#tiers was written to the address bar but never read back)
The top bar's section pills and view tabs got room to breathe, and a "?" next to the sections explains the 1/2/3 shortcuts on hover

Block series are visible as soon as you start one — the active series now sits on the champion-pool line at the top of Blocks, so a fresh two-week challenge shows up straight away instead of only appearing once a game exists

Series goals: each series carries its own Markdown goals, opened in a popup from the series bubble on any block (or the ✎ next to the active series). Write what the challenge is for, rename the series there, and older series keep their goals reachable from their own blocks

Strong side / weak side is now detected automatically: a block game's Side picker defaults to Auto and works it out from where your jungler started — you're strong side when they start on the map half opposite your lane. It also shows where both junglers began and what that made of your lane opponent, so a deficit can be read in context. You can still override it per game. New games get it automatically; run ./crawl.sh --backfill-jungle-sides to fill in older ones

Blocks: tell the app yourself whether you won the lane — each game's expanded panel gets a 'Lane result' picker (Stomped loss / Lost / Even / Won / Stomp win) for the 7m and 14m marks, set independently, plus a Strongside/Weakside flag. A result you set overrides that mark's lane column, for the games the automatic read gets wrong (a proactive dive, a disconnect, a gank the numbers can't see); leave it on Auto to keep the existing behaviour

New Tier list maker (own tab): drag any champion from the full roster into S/A/B/C/D tiers (rename/recolour tiers, add/remove rows), keep multiple named lists, and it all auto-saves and rides along in your backups. Thanks to @bs1phc

Tier lists can now be saved into a champion's Matchup guide: build one in the Tier list tab, pick a champion and hit 'Save to guide' — it shows up read-only on that champion's guide page (several per champion; re-saving the same list updates its copy). Plus a new '⇄ Compare' window that puts up to 4 tier lists side by side in a 2×2 layout. Thanks to @bs1phc
The tier-list champion pool can be filtered by role, with each champion's lane(s) worked out from the games you've crawled

Lowering the UI opacity no longer washes text out over a background picture — translucency now stops at a readable floor, and each view's content sits on its own surface panel instead of directly on the image. Thanks to @bs1phc

The Matchup guide has a search box for the matchup list, sorts matchups with notes/guides first (each group A→Z), and shows each row's tools (📄 One Pager, ⏱ Cooldowns, ⧉ Compare, ✎ Edit) on collapsed rows too, so you don't have to expand a matchup to reach them. Thanks to @bs1phc

The Matchup guide comparison shows what each research player actually ran per recent game — summoner spells, runes (with stat shards), the game-start buy and full build in purchase order, and the ability max order (Q>W>E) — in a clean columnar pop-out with a Show spells & items toggle (up to 6 players, 3 per row)

Lane Δ @14m (ΔCS / ΔGold vs the direct lane opponent) is shown for every compared player; comparison fetches pull match timelines again to make this and the item/skill data possible, and older stored games back-fill region-correctly on the next fetch
Summoner spells and items are captured on new crawls; run ./crawl.sh --backfill-items to fill them in for already-stored games

Compare yourself against other players — enable it in Settings → Research & comparison, add players by Riot ID, then hit the ⧉ button on a Matchup guide row to open a side-by-side view of their stats, runes and recent games in that matchup. Each player toggles on/off, and their games are fetched on demand (last 60 days by default, with a "Fetch more" button to widen the window). Thanks to @bs1phc for the contribution
Rune win rates on the Matchup guide — each matchup now shows your win rate by keystone and by secondary tree, drawn from the runes you actually ran in those games. Thanks to @bs1phc

General runes mode (Settings → Matchup guide) — switch from per-matchup rune pages to a single champion-level rune set shown by the item build. Your per-matchup pages aren't deleted; they reappear if you switch back. Thanks to @bs1phc
Remove a tracked account and purge its crawled data from Settings, while keeping your sessions, block learnings and notes. Thanks to @bs1phc
Table-heavy views (Matchups, Coaching progress, Trends, Blocks) now expand to fill the window when you widen it, so you can reveal more columns instead of scrolling sideways
Blue/red side filter added to the Matchups, Overview, Trends and Coaching-progress filter rows — see your stats for games where you were on a specific side
Fixed the Matchup guide not refreshing its game counts when you change the selected account (it needed a navigate-away-and-back before)

Live Lookup (📡 on the Matchup guide) — finds your live game, switches to the champion you're playing, and pops open the one-pager for the matchup so your notes are one click away. Riot's live API doesn't expose lane, so the opponent is guessed from your history with a quick enemy-champion switcher to correct it
Matchups: the column picker now adds/removes columns on the main matchups table (including metric averages like the lane Δ's), and an expanded game always shows every stat
Coaching progress: one column picker for the table — the lane Δ metrics are now available there as period averages; the expanded period panel always shows every stat
Renamed the block's "current" badge to "active"
Selectable date format in Settings — ISO (2026-07-20), US (7/20/2026, 12h) or EU (20/7/2026, 24h) — applied everywhere dates and times show

Block header redesigned: editable block name on the left (defaults to the block's date), its number beside it, the series shown as a bubble on the right, and the current block highlighted; the active series name now shows next to the + New series button

Click a column header to sort — on the Matchups table, the Overview champion breakdown and recent games, and the block games table. Click again to reverse; the block tables share one sort across every block

Block series — group blocks into a named run (e.g. a 2-week challenge) with a "+ New series" button on the Blocks page; each series names your blocks and numbers them from #1. Defaults to a generated "Since M/D/YYYY" title you can rename
Block numbers are now continuous — deleting a block and starting a new one no longer skips a number
Block series can be turned off in Settings — blocks then just number continuously as "#1, #2, …"

Blocks: the lane Δ (CS/level/gold at 7 & 14 min) are now selectable columns on the games table itself, next to result/opponent/KDA; the expanded per-game panel simply shows every stat (no separate column filter)
Blocks fetch the match timeline in the background to fill in those deeper lane stats, with a ⏳ marker on games still being crawled
New lane metrics measured directly vs your lane opponent from the match timeline: ΔCS, ΔLevel and ΔGold at ~7 and ~14 minutes — a truer 'was I ahead' signal than the old binary Riot laning flag

Every stats view (matchups, blocks, coaching progress, trends) now has a metric column picker; the new Δ metrics are off by default — tick them to show. New games capture the timeline automatically; run ./crawl.sh --backfill-lane-deltas to fill in past games
Fixed duplicate items in the item-build picker (some items appeared twice) — the list now shows one entry per item

One Pager (📄 on a Matchup guide row) — a full-screen, distraction-free quick reference for one matchup: runes, skill order, item build, and your notes. Made for a second screen during a game; Esc closes it
"Champ guide" is now "Matchup guide" throughout the app, with your champion's icon shown next to the selector

Back up everything you've written as one .zip (Settings → Export everything): sessions, block learnings, matchup guides incl. saved skill orders, champion notes, item builds, research entries, plus all uploaded clips and screenshots — and restore it on a fresh install via Import from a backup

Item build per champion on the guide page — core build order (up to 6 items) plus labeled situational sections, picked from real current-patch item icons; included in JSON export/import and the PDF export
Research tab — a study journal for other players' games: freeform Markdown entries (player, champion, opponent) with attached screenshots
Fixed Matchups rows getting stuck on "Loading…" when expanded (a function-name clash with the Champ guide silently broke the games fetch)
Cooldown popup's "💾 Save build" moved to the top-right corner of the dialog, next to the view toggle, where it's easy to spot

Champ guide reorganization: the guide editor now contains the skill order with nested edit/remove controls (read view shows it clean, no stray buttons); the cooldown popup's save is a compact 💾 Save in the skill-order header, fixing the misaligned Q/W/E/R rows between the two sides

Cooldown comparison gets a "Level matrix" view — level × ability grid where each rank-up bubble shows the ability's (haste-reduced) cooldown from that level on; cells stay clickable for editing the build, and the view choice is remembered

Skill order in the cooldown popup is now a full 18×4 grid (level × Q/W/E/R) — click a cell to spend that level's point, so 1-1-1 and 2-1-0 openers and anything else legal works; selections are validated against the in-game rules
Save your build per matchup: the cooldown popup's "Save build to champ guide" stores your skill order on that matchup's champ guide, preloads it next time, and shows it read-only on the guide page
Cooldown comparison (⏱) is also available on Champ guide matchup rows

Champion pool management moved to Settings (replacing the separate "My champion" setting — your pool's first pick is your default champion now); the Blocks view shows a read-only pool summary with an edit shortcut into Settings

Cooldown comparison popup (⏱ on a Matchups row) — your ability cooldowns side by side with the opponent's, with haste sources (items/runes/buffs granting ability haste or ultimate haste) reducing the shown values next to base
Each side has a champion level slider and a drag-to-reorder skill priority (R at 6/11/16) so cooldowns reflect actual ranks at that level — skill order is remembered per champion

Champion dropdowns (Champ guide, default champion, note migration) group your Champion Pool at the top, in pool priority order; the Champ guide also defaults to your pool's first pick when no default champion is set
Champion pool chips can be drag'n'drop reordered — order is the pool's priority (main first, counters in preference order) and is used wherever the pool appears
Champ guide list is table-like: aligned columns, row hover, and separate indicators for matchup notes (📝) and rune pages (🔮)
Fixed partially-filled rune pages silently failing to save (unfilled slots were rejected by validation with a near-invisible error)
Save failures in the Champ guide now show a clear red error message
Switching champion or collapsing a matchup mid-edit now asks before discarding unsaved changes
Rune pages in the Champ guide expand for viewing (▸ on the page card) — full rune names by tree, no need to open the editor
Matchups with a guide now always show in the Champ guide list, even against opponents that champion hasn't faced yet (e.g. migrated or imported notes)
Older matchup notes (pre-champ-guide) now surface in Settings — migrate them under one of your champions, or delete them (replaces the one-time startup popup)
Default champion setting — pre-selects your champion on the Champ guide page

Champ guide design pass: consistent Markdown editor, patch dropdown defaulting to the current patch (validated), properly sized champion icons, opponent picker only lists champions without a guide, clearer empty-state
Clips section design pass: add-clip form now folds behind a + Add clip button and matches the app's form styling
Fixed the Fiddlesticks champion icon never loading (match-v5 vs DDragon spelling mismatch)
One-time prompt after updating: matchup notes written before the champ-guide update are no longer shown in the app — answer yes to export them as Markdown files to a folder of your choice
Champ-guide import now validates rune pages and file structure (clear errors instead of accepting malformed files), and export rejects invalid champion names
Champ guide can be exported as a printable PDF — general notes, patch, rune pages (with icons), and notes for every matchup
Accent color customization in Settings — pick any color for buttons, active tabs, links, and chart lines
Appearance settings — adjustable opacity (see-through panels, like a translucent terminal) and an optional background picture
Runes actually played now show in a block game's expanded stats panel too, mirroring Overview and Champ guide
Removed the 10-game cap on block size — set any block size in Settings
Recent games (Overview and Champ guide) now show the game's time, not just the date
Fixed the packaged Windows app crashing on launch (AttributeError from uvicorn's logging setup touching a None stderr in the windowed/no-console build)
Overview tab's Recent games now records and shows the opponent's runes too, not just yours — click the ▸ Runes toggle on a game to compare both side by side
Crawler now also captures the lane opponent's runes (not just tracked accounts); run ./crawl.sh --backfill-runes again to fill in opponent runes for matches crawled before this update
Overview tab's Recent games table now shows the runes actually played per game
Attach short clips (upload a local video, or paste a YouTube/Twitch link) to a specific part of a coaching session or a specific game in a block — each clip gets its own label
Champ guide matchups are collapsed by default — click a matchup to expand its notes, runes, and recent games, instead of everything loading open at once
Recent games now only fetch when you expand a matchup, not for every matchup up front
Recent games in the Champ guide now show the full rune page actually played (keystone, minors, secondary tree, shards), not just the keystone
Champ guide's matchup rows show a "Recent games" column on the right — real games vs that opponent, with the runes you actually played in each one
Crawler now records the actual rune page played per game for tracked accounts; run `./crawl.sh --backfill-runes` to fill it in for matches crawled before this update
General notes section on the Champ guide page, for champion-wide tips that aren't tied to one matchup
Export/import a champion's whole guide as a JSON file, with an optional password (real encryption, not just obfuscation) — Export/Import menus on the Champ guide page

Champ guide moved to its own page — pick any champion (full roster, not just ones you've played) and see/edit full rune pages, patch, and notes for every matchup it has faced, or add one for a matchup you haven't played yet
Rune picker is now a full click-through builder — primary tree, keystone, 3 minor rows, secondary tree, 2 secondary minors, and 3 stat shards, with real rune icons
A matchup can hold more than one rune page (e.g. alternatives you're testing)
Champ guide is scoped per (your champion, opponent) instead of just the opponent — Gwen vs Darius and Camille vs Darius get separate guides
Matchups table links out to the Champ guide page for the selected "My champion" filter
Champ guide tab on matchups — record a rune keystone + secondary tree, patch version, and Markdown notes on how to play each matchup
Blocks auto-close when a newly added game is too far (game time) from the block's latest game — threshold in Settings (default 3 h, 0 = off), with an optional confirmation prompt (on by default)
Settings page grouped into sections with a sticky, more visible Save bar
Block notes in matchups render as Markdown (all notes now do, everywhere)
Patch notes panel — this one! 📋 in the top bar
Adjustable block size in Settings (1–10 games, default 3)
Matchups table marks champions that have block notes (🧱) alongside manual notes (📝)
Block notes in the matchup overview can expand the block's learnings inline
Account selector: multi-select dropdown in the top bar, works in every view, tier-colored, 'All accounts' default
Blocks can be closed early (with confirmation; irreversible)
Coaching sessions always shown in full; stats scope to the selected accounts
Block notes vs each champion shown inside the matchup overview, with links to their blocks
MIT license
'Hide my rank / LP' setting hides your own rank everywhere, including graphs
Matchup overview split into two columns: notes left, win/loss timeline right
Win/loss bars click through to that game's details
Rolling 10-game graph of lane won @7/@14 min per matchup
Matchups moved to their own tab with per-matchup notes (Markdown) and win/loss timeline
Rank chart estimates LP between snapshots from ranked wins/losses (fainter line)
Rank over time chart on the Overview with a vertical line for every coaching session
